Field notes · Session planning

Planning a proposal, quietly

A thoughtful plan for keeping the surprise and capturing the moment.

A surprise proposal is a lot to hold in your head. The aim of the photography plan is to make one part feel easy: knowing the moment will be documented while you stay with the person in front of you.

Begin with your partner.

Think about whether they would enjoy a public moment or a quieter setting. The location should fit the two of you. A meaningful place can matter more than an elaborate setup.

Talk through the exact spot.

We’ll discuss where you’ll arrive, where you’ll stand, and how I can see the moment without interrupting it. Share photographs or a simple description of the location, and have an alternative if the space is busy.

Leave a little room in the timeline.

Allow for traffic, a longer walk, or a pause along the way. Good communication helps more than a minute-by-minute script. We’ll agree on a signal and how to reach each other before you arrive.

Separate the photography from the setup.

If you want flowers, candles, an arch, or a picnic, plan who is arranging those details. Photography coverage doesn’t automatically include decorations or setup. Discuss any venue access, cleanup, and extra costs in advance.

Stay in the moment afterward.

You don’t have to turn immediately toward the camera. Take the time you need together. Afterward, we can make a few portraits, photograph the ring, and remember the setting where it happened.

Have a weather plan, a private way to communicate, and a pocket that keeps the ring secure. Then leave space for the moment to be its own.
